result.title: Oscillatory Neural Dynamics over Sheaves
result.summary: Effective long-range propagation remains a central challenge in graph neural networks, as increasing a model's propagation depth does not guarantee that distant nodes effectively influence each other. Sheaf neural networks enrich graph propagation through matrix-valued transport between stalks; still, this expressivity alone does not automatically imply effective long-range communication. We introduce ONDA, a long-range graph learning framework based on operator-valued information waves. Stalk-valued representations evolve through second-order dynamics governed by learned sheaf transport operators, combining wave-like propagation with expressive local geometry. We characterize long-range influence through a stalk-wise sensitivity analysis and show that the cross-influence never vanishes. Across long-range propagation, severe graph bottlenecks, graph transfer, and heterophilic benchmarks, ONDA consistently improves over scalar wave propagation, diffusive sheaf baselines, and state-of-the-art models, demonstrating the benefit of coupling wave dynamics with matrix-valued transport.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文提出 ONDA 框架，把图上的表征视为茎空间（stalk）取值，用学习到的 sheaf 传输算子驱动二阶波动动力学，让远距离节点之间保持非零的跨节点影响，并在长程传播与异质图等基准上验证。
AI.relevance_reason: 其“矩阵值传输 + 二阶状态演化 + 灵敏度刻画远距离影响不消失”可类比 LVR 中 latent 推理状态的更新算子与长程信息保留问题，可能为分析 latent 表示坍缩与深度泛化提供工具，但需核查其是否只针对图结构而无视觉推理设置。
